headline: High: Authelia’s broad egress plus Great Expectations’ file-based validation can create unsafe data-flow and compliance exposure, while prompt-injection risk is low without a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, Great Expectations reads files and Authelia can emit network-backed auth flows; if operators bridge them via copied config or shared files, malicious content could influence downstream interpretation. This is a pairwise, not intrinsic, risk.
conditions: IF the operator copies Authelia-generated content into Great Expectations config or docs files
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted content into validation configs
Review any imported text before running Great Expectations
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results, documentation, and data sources via files, while Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth APIs. If sensitive data enters the shared workflow, Authelia can move it off-host through its network path. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default data-engineering setups.
conditions: IF sensitive data is written into files that Great Expectations processes
IF Authelia is configured to forward or relay those artifacts over networked auth flows
mitigations: Restrict sensitive datasets from Great Expectations inputs
Run Authelia without access to those files
Separate credentials and workspaces per agent
Audit outbound destinations for Authelia
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write capability is listed, while Great Expectations can install packages and read/write validation files. There is no documented overlapping write target or shared mutable resource, so direct conflict is limited unless an operator places both on the same writable directory.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF package installation by Great Expectations modifies artifacts Authelia also consumes
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Pin package versions before running validations
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Make Authelia inputs read-only
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation that can be treated as authoritative, and Authelia can act on networked auth flows. If Authelia consumes Great Expectations outputs without verification, a bad validation result can cascade into incorrect access or deployment decisions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Authelia or an operator treats Great Expectations output as authoritative
IF validation results are used to gate auth or deployment actions without review
mitigations: Require human review of validation outputs
Add a second verification step before acting
Separate validation from authorization decisions
Log provenance for each result
requires-engineering: implement policy checks before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations explicitly handles validation results and documentation, while Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces. If regulated data is validated in Great Expectations and then forwarded through Authelia, retention or residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are processed by Great Expectations
IF Authelia forwards related records to a jurisdiction or service with different retention rules
mitigations: Classify data before running either agent
Keep regulated data out of shared validation flows
Document retention for validation artifacts
Review outbound auth logs for residency issues
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
